hypotheses.persona: A healthcare worker (likely a nurse or doctor) who works a day shift on weekdays, with a different schedule on Friday (possibly half-day) and a relaxed weekend routine. The weekday pattern includes returning home around 18:00, changing out of scrubs, and placing work items (badge, stethoscope, keys, phone, thermos) in a designated 'elsewhere' area. On Saturday and Sunday, the routine is more leisurely: breakfast at 08:06, early dinner at 17:51-18:09, and evening relaxation with phone at sofa and nightstand. No work items appear on weekends, consistent with days off. — Day 11 (Friday) shows keys at entry_hook at 12:04 (early return, consistent with half-day), then keys at nightstand at 13:53 (likely placed after coming home). No other work items (badge, stethoscope, scrubs) appear, which is unusual but could be due to a different routine on Friday (e.g., not wearing scrubs, or items stored elsewhere). The morning routine (phone and water_bottle at nightstand at 07:30, bowl at table at 07:57, bowl at sink at 08:21) is consistent with breakfast before work. The evening relaxation (remote at sofa at 19:41, phone at nightstand at 22:11) matches weekend pattern. The water_bottle at nightstand at 18:47 is consistent with evening hydration.
hypotheses.rationale: The early return on Friday (keys at entry_hook at 12:04) strongly supports the half-day hypothesis. The absence of work items after work is puzzling but could be due to a different routine (e.g., not wearing scrubs on Friday, or items stored elsewhere). The morning and evening patterns are consistent with previous days. The probability is slightly reduced because of the missing work items, but the overall pattern remains strong.

hypotheses.rationale: The early return on Friday (keys at entry_hook at 12:04) could also be explained by a half-day at a non-healthcare job, but the absence of work items (badge, stethoscope, scrubs) on other days is not explained. The probability is reduced further because the early return is more consistent with a half-day work schedule than a general structured routine.
